cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: GCSE Latin verse set texts are prescribed by each exam board and change every two years. Check which texts are current for your exam year.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Common verse authors include Virgil (Aeneid), Ovid (Metamorphoses), Catullus (poems), and Horace (Odes and Satires).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Virgil's Aeneid is the national epic of Rome, telling how Aeneas fled Troy and founded the Roman race in Italy. Key themes: pietas, fate, the cost of empire.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Ovid's Metamorphoses tells myths of transformation, often with wit, irony, and playful subversion of epic conventions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Catullus wrote personal lyric poetry about love, friendship, and social satire. His poems to Lesbia are among the most famous love poetry in any language.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Horace's Odes are polished, philosophical lyrics reflecting on life, death, love, and Roman values with understated elegance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: The Aeneid was written under Augustus (29-19 BC) and explores the tension between personal happiness and public duty.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Ovid was exiled by Augustus; the Metamorphoses (AD 8) can be read as subtly questioning Augustan values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Understanding metre is essential: the hexameter is the metre of epic, while lyric poets use various metres (Sapphic, Alcaic, elegiac couplet).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Verse Set Texts
cards.back: Each board prescribes approximately 110-120 lines of verse text for detailed study of translation, analysis, and evaluation.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse latin exam tips — verse set texts?
cards.back: 1. For Verse Set Texts, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Verse Set Texts, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
Compare how Virgil and Ovid approach the theme of power in their verse set texts. (8 marks)
